examples.en: The police dragnet is closing in.

examples.ko: 범인은 수사망을 피해 계속 도망 다녔어요.
examples.en: The culprit kept running to avoid the dragnet.

examples.ko: 수사망에 걸린 사람이 벌써 세 명이에요.
examples.en: Three people have already been caught in the dragnet.

examples.ko: 이번 사건은 수사망을 넓혀서 다시 조사하기로 했어요.
examples.en: For this case, they decided to widen the dragnet and investigate again.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 수사망 밖에 있어서 아무 일도 없었어요.
examples.en: He was outside the dragnet, so nothing happened to him.
The news said the dragnet has spread across the whole country.

explain: '수사망이 좁혀지다', '수사망을 피하다', '수사망에 걸리다'처럼 짝말로 외워 두면 좋아요. 뉴스와 기사에 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '경찰이 쫓고 있어요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is good to learn it in set phrases such as '수사망이 좁혀지다' (the dragnet closes in), '수사망을 피하다' (avoid the dragnet) and '수사망에 걸리다' (get caught in the dragnet). It appears a lot in news and articles, while in daily talk people say things like '경찰이 쫓고 있어요' (the police are after him).

examples.en: The investigation team arrived at the scene and started looking into it.

examples.ko: 경찰은 수사진을 두 배로 늘리기로 했어요.
examples.en: The police decided to double the size of the investigation team.

examples.ko: 새로 꾸린 수사진에 전문가가 여러 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are several experts on the newly formed investigation team.
According to the investigators, the results will come out soon.

examples.ko: 이 사건은 수사진도 처음 보는 경우라고 해요.
examples.en: They say even the investigators have never seen a case like this.
The whole investigation team checked the materials all night.

explain: '의료진', '취재진', '경영진'처럼 '-진'이 붙어서 사람들의 팀 전체를 가리켜요. 한 사람은 '수사관'이라고 하고, 뉴스에서는 '수사진이 꾸려지다', '수사진을 보강하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Like '의료진' (medical staff), '취재진' (press corps) and '경영진' (management), the '-진' ending refers to a whole team of people. One person is called '수사관' (investigator). In the news you often see '수사진이 꾸려지다' (a team is formed) and '수사진을 보강하다' (reinforce the team).

examples.en: That person's behavior is a bit suspicious.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 우리 집 앞을 서성이는 사람이 수상쩍었어요.
examples.en: The person hanging around in front of my house late at night looked suspicious.
I got a suspicious call, so I didn't answer.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 값이 너무 싸서 수상쩍다고 생각했어요.
examples.en: The prices at that shop were so cheap that I thought it was fishy.

examples.ko: 왜 갑자기 친절하게 구는지 수상쩍지 않아요?
examples.en: Doesn't it seem suspicious why he's suddenly being so nice?

examples.ko: 수상쩍게 웃더니 아무 말도 안 하고 나갔어요.
examples.en: He smiled suspiciously and went out without saying a word.

explain: 그냥 이상한 게 아니라 '뭔가 나쁜 일이 있는 것 같다'는 의심이 들어 있어요. '수상하다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰는데, '수상쩍다'는 의심스러운 느낌을 조금 더 강하게 말할 때 어울려요. '수상쩍은 사람', '수상쩍게 굴다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is not just 'strange' but carries a doubt that something bad might be going on. '수상하다' is used with a similar meaning, and '수상쩍다' suits a slightly stronger feeling of suspicion. Typical uses are '수상쩍은 사람' (a suspicious person) and '수상쩍게 굴다' (act suspiciously).

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 선생님이 저를 수상히 쳐다보셨어요.
examples.en: During class, the teacher looked at me suspiciously.
My younger sibling went into the room with a suspicious smile.

examples.ko: 경비 아저씨가 낯선 사람을 수상히 여겼어요.
examples.en: The security guard found the stranger suspicious.
I don't know why you're acting so suspiciously.
The kids were suspiciously quiet, so I went to check on them.

examples.ko: 문 앞에서 수상히 서성이는 남자가 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a man lingering suspiciously in front of the door.

explain: '수상히 여기다', '수상히 보다'처럼 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '수상하게'라고 말해요. '수상쩍게'로 바꿔도 뜻이 통해요.
explain_en: It often appears in writing and the news as '수상히 여기다' (find suspicious) or '수상히 보다' (look at suspiciously). In daily conversation people usually say '수상하게'. Swapping in '수상쩍게' also works.

examples.en: The chief delegate's speech was very long.
The chief delegate leaves on tomorrow morning's flight.
They say a new chief negotiator has been appointed.
The chief delegates of the two countries met and shook hands.
The person who came as chief delegate is a former diplomat.
The chief delegate answered the question personally.

explain: 여러 명으로 이루어진 대표단에서 가장 높은 대표를 말할 때 써요. 회담, 협상, 국제회의 뉴스에 주로 나오고 '수석대표가 이끄는 대표단'처럼 '대표단'과 함께 자주 써요. 사람을 높일 때는 '수석대표님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Used for the top representative within a delegation of several people. It mostly appears in news about talks, negotiations and international conferences, often alongside '대표단' (delegation), as in '수석대표가 이끄는 대표단'. To show respect, say '수석대표님'.

examples.en: Even the country house now has a flush toilet.
It used to be very inconvenient because it wasn't a flush toilet.
The campsite restroom was clean because it had flush toilets.
The flush toilet got clogged, so I called someone.
My grandmother's house still doesn't have a flush toilet.

examples.ko: 수세식으로 바꾸는 공사를 다음 달에 해요.
examples.en: The work to switch to a flush toilet is next month.

explain: 보통 '수세식 화장실', '수세식 변기'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 물로 씻어 내리지 않는 옛날 방식은 '재래식 화장실'이라고 해서 둘을 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is usually placed before a noun, as in '수세식 화장실' or '수세식 변기'. The old-style toilet without flushing is called '재래식 화장실', so it helps to remember the two as a pair.

examples.en: In the negotiation, we were put in a defensive position.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 수세적 경기를 하다가 한 골을 먹었어요.
examples.en: Our team played defensively and then conceded a goal.

examples.ko: 너무 수세적 태도로는 문제를 풀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't solve the problem with an overly defensive attitude.

examples.ko: 수세적 자세만 지키지 말고 먼저 제안해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't just stay on the defensive; try making the first proposal.
The company is switching to a defensive strategy.

examples.ko: 그는 수세적인 말투로 자기 잘못이 아니라고 했어요.
examples.en: He said in a defensive tone that it wasn't his fault.

explain: 반대말은 '공세적'이에요. '수세적 입장', '수세적 태도'처럼 명사 앞에 쓰고, '수세적인', '수세적이다'로도 써요. 협상, 경기, 토론처럼 맞서는 상황에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: The opposite is '공세적' (offensive). It goes before a noun, as in '수세적 입장' or '수세적 태도', and also appears as '수세적인' or '수세적이다'. It is common in confrontational situations such as negotiations, sports and debates.

examples.en: The volume carried by rail has increased a lot this year.

examples.ko: 명절에는 택배 수송량은 평소의 두 배예요.
examples.en: During the holidays, parcel delivery volume is double the usual.
I'm worried because the port's shipping volume has dropped.
We need more trucks to increase the transport volume.
Compared with ships, planes carry less and cost more.
I looked up how much is transported per day.

explain: 사람이나 물건을 실어 나른 양을 숫자로 말할 때 써요. '화물 수송량', '여객 수송량'처럼 앞에 무엇을 나르는지 붙이는 경우가 많고, 뉴스와 경제 기사에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when talking about how much of people or goods was carried, in numbers. A word for what is carried often comes before it, as in '화물 수송량' (freight volume) and '여객 수송량' (passenger volume), and it shows up often in news and economic articles.

en: sit on one's hands; sit by idly

examples.ko: 친구가 어려운 일을 당했는데 수수방관할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: My friend is in trouble, so I can't just sit by.
The government was criticized for sitting idly by on the problem.

examples.ko: 회사는 직원의 불만을 계속 수수방관하고 있어요.
examples.en: The company keeps ignoring its employees' complaints.

examples.ko: 우리 모두 수수방관하지 말고 같이 도와요.
examples.en: Let's all stop standing by and help together.
I think an attitude of standing idly by is wrong.

examples.ko: 그 일을 수수방관한 사람은 아무도 없었어요.
examples.en: Nobody stood idly by on that matter.

explain: '~을 수수방관하다'처럼 목적어와 함께 쓰고, 나서서 도와야 할 사람이 가만히 있는 것을 비판할 때 많이 써요. 가벼운 말로는 '모른 척하다'가 있어요. 뉴스나 토론에서는 '수수방관하지 말고 대책을 세워야 한다'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used with an object, as in '~을 수수방관하다', and mostly criticizes someone who should step in and help but stays still. A lighter expression is '모른 척하다' (pretend not to know). In news and debates you often see lines like '수수방관하지 말고 대책을 세워야 한다' (they must make plans instead of standing by).

en: red bean and sorghum rice cake

examples.en: We always prepare susupat-tteok for a child's first birthday party.
My grandmother made susupat-tteok for me.
Susupat-tteok is red on the outside and chewy.

examples.ko: 생일마다 수수팥떡을 해 주시던 어머니가 생각나요.
examples.en: I remember my mother who made susupat-tteok every birthday.
I shared susupat-tteok with the neighbors.
The susupat-tteok is still warm, so it's delicious.

explain: 아이의 돌잔치나 생일에 해 주는 떡으로 알려져 있어요. 붉은 팥과 수수의 붉은색이 나쁜 기운을 막아 준다는 믿음에서 만든다고 해요. 한국 음식이나 풍습 이야기에서 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is known as a rice cake made for a child's first birthday party or birthdays. It is said to be made from the belief that the red color of red beans and sorghum keeps bad energy away. You may meet it when talking about Korean food and customs.

examples.ko: 뒤꼍에 선 수양버들이 햇볕을 받아 눈부시게 아름다웠어요.
examples.en: The weeping willow standing in the backyard was dazzlingly beautiful in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 강가에 늘어선 수양버들 가지가 바람에 흔들려요.
examples.en: The branches of the weeping willows lining the riverside sway in the wind.
In spring, light green leaves sprout on the weeping willow.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 공원에 수양버들 한 그루가 있어요.
examples.en: There is one weeping willow in my neighborhood park.
I waited for my friend under the weeping willow.
A weeping willow's branches droop down.

explain: 버드나무 가운데 가지가 아래로 길게 늘어지는 나무를 말해요. 평소에는 그냥 '버드나무'라고도 부르고, 시나 노래, 그림에서 강가나 봄 풍경으로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a kind of willow whose branches hang long and low. In everyday speech people may also just say '버드나무' (willow), and it often appears in poems, songs and paintings as part of a riverside or spring scene.

examples.en: In winter, the demand for heating rises a lot.
When prices go up, the quantity demanded usually falls.
The demand for rice this year is lower than last year.

examples.ko: 수요량을 정확히 알아야 물건을 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to know the demand exactly to make the products.
Demand for masks suddenly rose, so they sold out.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 수요량에 맞춰 빵을 구워요.
examples.en: This shop bakes bread to match the demand.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '공급량'이에요. 그냥 '수요'는 사려는 마음이나 필요를 넓게 말하고, '수요량'은 얼마나 필요한지 양으로 말할 때 써요. 경제 수업이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '공급량' (quantity supplied). Plain '수요' (demand) speaks broadly of the wish or need to buy, while '수요량' is for how much is needed, as an amount. It often appears in economics classes and the news.

examples.ko: 이 제품의 주요 수요층은 이십 대예요.
examples.en: The main consumer group for this product is people in their twenties.
We have to find a new consumer group for sales to grow.
There are more products aimed at elderly consumers.
Because of the high price, the customer base is limited.

examples.ko: 이 책은 수요층이 넓어서 잘 팔려요.
examples.en: This book sells well because it has a wide audience.
The tastes of the consumer group are changing quickly.

explain: '고객층', '소비자층'과 비슷하게 어떤 물건을 사려는 사람들의 무리를 말해요. '-층'이 붙어서 '독자층', '이용객층'처럼 사람 집단을 나타내는 말이 많아요. '수요층이 두텁다'처럼 많고 탄탄하다는 느낌으로도 써요.
explain_en: Like '고객층' and '소비자층', it refers to a group of people who want to buy a certain thing. The '-층' ending forms many words for groups of people, such as '독자층' (readership). It is also used as in '수요층이 두텁다' (the customer base is solid) to suggest a large, stable group.

examples.ko: 그는 새로운 의견에 수용적 태도를 보여요.
examples.en: He shows a receptive attitude toward new opinions.
Try listening to criticism with a receptive attitude.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 수용적인 분이라 말하기 편해요.
examples.en: My team leader is open to ideas, so it's easy to talk to them.
Children need to grow up in an accepting atmosphere.
It's not easy to listen that openly.
It's hard to have a conversation with someone who isn't receptive.

explain: 반대말은 '배타적'이에요. 사람의 성격이나 태도를 말할 때 '수용적 태도', '수용적인 사람'처럼 쓰고, '수용적이다', '수용적으로'로도 써요. 남의 말이나 새로운 것을 열린 마음으로 받아들인다는 칭찬의 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '배타적' (exclusive, closed). It describes a person's character or attitude, as in '수용적 태도' or '수용적인 사람', and also appears as '수용적이다' and '수용적으로'. It has a positive feel of taking in others' words and new things with an open mind.

examples.en: This job is harder than I thought.
Moving by yourself is no easy task.
Preparing for the exam was tough, so I stayed up all night.
It won't be easy, but give it a try.
Solving that problem wasn't easy.
If you give up because it's hard, you can't do anything.

explain: '수월하지 않다'가 줄어든 꼴이라 '쉽지 않다'와 비슷해요. 반대말은 '수월하다'예요. 말할 때는 '쉽지 않아요'가 더 흔하고, '수월찮다'는 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말투에서 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a contracted form of '수월하지 않다', so it is close to '쉽지 않다' (not easy). Its opposite is '수월하다' (easy). In speech '쉽지 않아요' is more common, while '수월찮다' is seen in writing or a slightly formal tone.

examples.en: I solved the problem easily, so I felt good.
Thanks to the directions, I found the place easily.

examples.ko: 준비를 미리 하면 수월히 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you prepare in advance, you can finish smoothly.
I thought it would be settled easily, but it wasn't.
I'm glad the child fell asleep without trouble.

examples.ko: 이 앱을 쓰면 수월히 예약할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use this app, you can book easily.

explain: '수월하게'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 보통 '수월하게'나 '쉽게'를 더 많이 써요. '수월히'는 글에서 자연스러워요. 반대는 '힘들게'나 '어렵게'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '수월하게', and in speech people usually say '수월하게' or '쉽게' more. '수월히' sounds natural in writing. The opposite would be '힘들게' or '어렵게'.

examples.en: This morning the temperature dropped below zero.
Today the temperature went over thirty degrees.
The mercury column goes up when the temperature rises.

examples.ko: 한파로 수은주가 뚝 떨어져서 두꺼운 옷을 입었어요.
examples.en: The cold wave made the temperature plunge, so I wore thick clothes.

examples.ko: 옛날 온도계의 수은주를 보며 열을 쟀어요.
examples.en: I took my temperature by looking at the mercury column of an old thermometer.

examples.ko: 수은주 눈금이 잘 안 보여서 안경을 썼어요.
examples.en: I couldn't see the mercury scale well, so I put on glasses.

explain: 뉴스에서는 '수은주가 떨어지다', '수은주가 오르다'처럼 기온이 변하는 것을 말할 때 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '기온이 떨어지다', '날씨가 추워지다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 갑자기 수은주가 뚝 떨어져서 패딩을 꺼냈어요.
phrases.en: The temperature suddenly plunged, so I took out my padded jacket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 수은 기둥이 아니라 '기온'을 가리켜요. 뉴스나 기사에서 날씨가 급히 추워질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the temperature, not to an actual mercury column. News and articles use it when the weather turns cold quickly.

explain_en: In the news it is often used as '수은주가 떨어지다' or '수은주가 오르다' to talk about temperature changes. In daily conversation people say '기온이 떨어지다' or '날씨가 추워지다' instead.

examples.en: I want to study veterinary science at university.

examples.ko: 수의학과에 들어가려면 점수가 아주 높아야 해요.
examples.en: You need very high scores to get into the veterinary department.
A friend who majored in veterinary science opened an animal hospital.
I hear that in veterinary science you learn about cows and horses too.
Veterinary science is popular these days because there are more pets.

examples.ko: 형은 수의학 박사 과정에 다니고 있어요.
examples.en: My older brother is in a doctoral program in veterinary science.

explain: 동물의 병을 보는 사람은 '수의사'라고 하고, 사람의 병을 다루는 공부는 '의학'이라고 해요. 대학에서는 '수의학과'나 '수의과대학'이라는 이름을 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: A person who treats animal illnesses is called a '수의사' (veterinarian), while the study of human illness is '의학' (medicine). At universities you will see the names '수의학과' or '수의과대학'.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 수적으로 불리했지만 끝까지 싸웠어요.
examples.en: Our team was at a numerical disadvantage but fought to the end.

examples.ko: 수적 우위를 믿고 방심하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't let your guard down just because you outnumber them.
In terms of numbers, we have far more people.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 수적 열세를 극복하고 이겼어요.
examples.en: Our team overcame being outnumbered and won.
The difference in numbers is not big.
Qualitative change is more important than change in numbers.

explain: '수적 우위', '수적 열세'처럼 명사 앞에 쓰고, '수적으로'의 꼴로 많이 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '질적'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '숫자상으로', '숫자로는'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '수적 우위' (numerical superiority) and '수적 열세' (numerical disadvantage), and is often used in the form '수적으로'. Its counterpart is '질적' (qualitative). In daily talk people also say '숫자상으로' or '숫자로는'.

examples.en: That boss is a well-known miser.

examples.ko: 돈을 안 쓴다고 나를 수전노라고 불러요.
examples.en: They call me a miser because I don't spend money.

examples.ko: 수전노처럼 굴지 말고 밥 한 번 사세요.
examples.en: Don't act like a miser; buy us a meal for once.
The miser in the story ended up lonely.

examples.ko: 그 수전노 영감이 동전 하나도 안 내놓았어요.
examples.en: That miserly old man didn't hand over even a single coin.
Even a miser would spend money on family, right?

explain: '구두쇠', '짠돌이'와 비슷하지만 돈에만 집착한다고 비난하는 느낌이 있어서 사람 앞에서 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 가볍게 놀릴 때는 '짠돌이'나 '구두쇠'를 더 많이 써요. 이야기나 속담 속 인물에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is close to '구두쇠' and '짠돌이', but it carries a tone of blaming someone for caring only about money, so saying it to a person can be rude. For light teasing, '짠돌이' or '구두쇠' are used more. It also often appears for characters in stories and sayings.

examples.en: My grandfather has a hand tremor.

examples.ko: 커피를 많이 마셨더니 수전증처럼 손이 떨려요.
examples.en: After drinking a lot of coffee, my hands shake as if I had a tremor.
Because of my hand tremor, it's hard to write.
A hand tremor can get worse as people get older.
My hand tremor was bad, so I went to the hospital.
I'm taking medicine to treat my hand tremor.

explain: '불면증', '건망증'처럼 '-증'이 붙은 병이나 증상 이름이에요. 긴장해서 잠깐 손이 떨리는 것은 '손이 떨리다'라고 하고, 오래 계속되는 증상을 말할 때 '수전증'이라고 해요. '수전증이 있다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the name of a condition or symptom with '-증' attached, like '불면증' (insomnia) and '건망증' (forgetfulness). A short bout of shaking from nerves is just '손이 떨리다', while '수전증' is for a symptom that keeps going. It is used as '수전증이 있다'.

examples.ko: 닭의 수정란은 따뜻하게 두면 병아리가 돼요.
examples.en: A chicken's fertilized egg becomes a chick if kept warm.
In science class, we observed frog fertilized eggs.
The fertilized egg grows as its cells divide.

examples.ko: 수정란 하나가 쌍둥이로 나뉘는 경우도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes a single fertilized egg splits into twins.
A new life begins inside the fertilized egg.
When I shone a light on the fertilized egg, I could see inside.

explain: 과학이나 생물 수업에서 주로 쓰는 말이에요. 먹는 달걀 가운데 수정이 된 것은 '유정란'이라고 해서 식품 이야기에서는 이 말을 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly a word for science and biology classes. Among eggs people eat, one that has been fertilized is called a '유정란', which is the word used when talking about food.

examples.en: The lens of the eye is similar to a camera lens.

examples.ko: 나이가 들면 수정체가 뿌옇게 변하기도 해요.
examples.en: As people get older, the lens of the eye can become cloudy.
The thickness of the lens changes to adjust focus.

examples.ko: 수정체 수술을 받은 할머니가 잘 보인다고 하세요.
examples.en: My grandmother, who had lens surgery, says she can see well.

examples.ko: 눈이 나빠지는 건 수정체와도 관계가 있어요.
examples.en: Worsening eyesight also has to do with the lens.
Be careful with ultraviolet rays to protect the lens of your eye.

explain: '각막', '홍채', '망막'처럼 눈의 구조를 배울 때 함께 나와요. 백내장은 이 수정체가 뿌옇게 되는 병이에요. 안경이나 콘택트 '렌즈'와 달리 눈 안에 있는 부분을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It comes up together with '각막' (cornea), '홍채' (iris) and '망막' (retina) when learning the structure of the eye. A cataract ('백내장') is a condition where this lens becomes cloudy. Unlike a glasses or contact '렌즈', it is the part inside the eye.

examples.en: He is the top pupil of a famous painter.
The master handed the shop down to his best pupil.
I learned so hard that I could be called the best pupil.

examples.ko: 우리 스승님의 수제자가 오늘 강연을 해요.
examples.en: Our teacher's best pupil is giving a lecture today.
It's not easy to be recognized as the best pupil.

examples.ko: 제가 무슨 수제자는 아니지만 열심히 배웠어요.
examples.en: I'm not exactly the best pupil, but I learned diligently.

explain: 스승 밑의 여러 제자 중에서 가장 뛰어난 제자를 말해요. 스승이 사랑하고 아끼는 제자를 말하는 '애제자'와는 달라서, '수제자'는 실력이 으뜸이라는 느낌이 더 강해요. 무술, 예술, 학문처럼 스승에게 배우는 분야에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the most outstanding pupil among a master's students. It differs from '애제자' (a beloved pupil), since '수제자' leans more toward being top in skill. It is often used in fields learned from a master, such as martial arts, the arts and scholarship.

examples.en: The shipyard's order amount has grown a lot this year.

examples.ko: 이번 계약 덕분에 수주액도 일 조 원을 넘었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to this contract, the order total also exceeded one trillion won.

examples.ko: 수주액은 작년보다 두 배 가까이 올랐어요.
examples.en: The order amount rose nearly double compared to last year.
The company announced its overseas order amount.
The order amount has dropped, so the employees are worried.
The bonus varies depending on the order amount.

explain: 주문을 받는 것은 '수주', 주문을 내는 것은 '발주'라서 둘을 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. '수주액'은 주문을 받은 금액이고, 건설·조선·수출 같은 경제 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 동사는 '수주하다'예요.
explain_en: Receiving an order is '수주' and placing one is '발주', so it helps to remember the two as a pair. '수주액' is the amount of money from orders received, and it often appears in economic news about construction, shipbuilding and exports. The verb is '수주하다'.

examples.en: I think this movie is really a quality work.

examples.ko: 올해 나온 소설 중에서 수준작을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked out a quality piece from the novels released this year.
The exhibition had many fine works, so it was worth seeing.
Critics picked this drama as a quality work.

examples.ko: 수준작인데도 사람들이 잘 모르는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It's a fine work, yet it seems people don't know it well.

examples.ko: 첫 작품이 수준작이라서 다음 작품이 기대돼요.
examples.en: Since the first work was so good, I'm looking forward to the next.

explain: 영화, 소설, 드라마, 전시 같은 작품이 꽤 잘 만들어졌다고 칭찬할 때 써요. 보통 '걸작'이나 '명작'보다 가볍고 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. '수준작으로 꼽히다', '수준작이라고 평가하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Used to praise a work such as a film, novel, drama or exhibit as well made. It is usually lighter and more casual than '걸작' (masterpiece) or '명작' (classic). Common uses are '수준작으로 꼽히다' (be counted as a quality work) and '수준작이라고 평가하다' (evaluate as a quality work).
